title: Key-person dependence and succession
status_rationale: Business plan section 11.09 explicitly treats founder dependence as concentration risk but is a draft policy position with no succession arrangements, designated successor or tested continuity located. Echelon is very small and is likely dependent on one principal.
target_answer: We treat key-person dependence as a primary risk and mitigate it with mechanisms that work without the principal: (1) the operating agreement designates a successor manager with springing authority on death or incapacity; (2) break-glass credentials for cloud, domain, code hosting and signing keys are held in sealed custody by a named second party, with access logged and tested annually; (3) source code, infrastructure definitions, deployment runbooks and data export tooling are deposited with an escrow agent and verified by an independent build test; (4) customer data is always exportable by the customer without Echelon involvement; (5) Praxis records keep decisions, research and handoffs durable outside any person's memory or an AI conversation; (6) key-person life and disability insurance funds an orderly transition. We report the number of people holding each critical capability.
current_practice: Not established. The organization appears to depend on a single principal; no successor, credential custody, escrow or continuity test was located.
intended_practice: Implement the six mechanisms before the first production customer, prioritizing credential custody, escrow and customer-controlled export.
provable: Nothing operational. Praxis handoff and provenance tooling exists in repositories but no continuity test has been performed.
customer_statement: Echelon is an early-stage company with significant dependence on its founder. A succession and continuity plan including escrow, credential custody and customer-controlled data export is planned but not yet in place.
residual_risks: Escrow and documentation do not transfer tacit judgment; a successor operator would still need ramp-up time.
Sealed credential custody creates its own insider risk at the custodian.
open_questions: Who would be the designated successor or credential custodian?

challenge.customer_intent: Assurance that the service, data and contract survive the loss of the founder.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Service stops, data is inaccessible, or no one can lawfully act for the vendor after the founder's death, incapacity or departure.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Conventional answers (organization charts, cross-training, key-person insurance) address larger firms; for a one-person company cross-training is impossible and insurance pays the company, not the customer.
challenge.legally_required: No statute requires succession planning by a vendor; banking supervisory guidance expects institutions to consider vendor continuity and key personnel.
challenge.contractually_required: Commonly requested in enterprise and bank contracts through business continuity, escrow and termination assistance clauses.
challenge.historical_convention: Buyers ask for headcount and succession plans and often exclude single-founder vendors from critical activities.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Customer-held, always-exportable data and a design in which Unbound never holds funds (CNV-LEG-001) remove the most severe consequences of vendor failure.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Release gate that fails when the export round-trip or escrow build verification fails.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Per-release export test results, escrow deposit verification reports and an annual tested credential break-glass record.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Verified escrow plus customer-controlled export plus designated successor authority, instead of relying on headcount.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, by an escrow agent's verification report and a customer-observed export and restore test.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Escrow deposits not refreshed per release; credentials rotated without updating custody; export format not importable by any alternative system.
challenge.conventional_cost: Hiring additional staff to remove dependence: high and not feasible at this stage.
challenge.alternative_cost: Escrow agent fees and verification testing plus legal drafting: medium, order-of-magnitude judgment, not sourced.
challenge.alternative_risks: Custodian compromise; false comfort if no successor operator actually exists.
supporting_arguments: Escrow and export address the customer's real loss scenario directly.
Evidence is producible on a schedule rather than asserted.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Uncertain. Some banks will not accept any single-founder vendor for a critical activity regardless of mitigations; DAF sponsors and smaller institutions may accept verified escrow and export.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Regulators and bank TPRM teams weigh organizational depth explicitly and may treat these as insufficient.
A successor operator with the right F# and PostgreSQL skills may not be readily available.

title: Policy governance: adoption, review, publication and enforceability
status_rationale: The only located policy is the Echelon Secure Construction Standard v0.1, explicitly proposed and not adopted. No policy register, approval record or review cadence exists.
target_answer: Every policy is a versioned record with owner, approver, approval date, effective date, next review date and the controls and checks that enforce each rule. Policies are adopted by the managing member and reviewed at least annually or on material change. title: Conflicts of interest and related-party relationships with sponsors
status_rationale: Business plan section 14.05 is a draft policy position on conflicts. DAF landscape research documents sponsor boards that include vendor personnel and related-party vendor fees, so sponsors and their auditors will ask. No conflict policy or disclosure register exists at Echelon.
target_answer: Echelon maintains a conflict-of-interest policy covering owners, personnel and contractors, with annual and event-driven disclosure, and a register of every role an Echelon person holds at a customer, grantee, investment manager, custodian or competitor. We disclose to each sponsor any relationship that could make an Echelon person an interested person for Form 990 Schedule L or a disqualified person for section 4958, and provide the information the sponsor needs for its own analysis. status_rationale: Unbound convergence clauses define the intended regulatory posture: Unbound does not hold or move donor or grant money and cannot execute payments (CNV-LEG-001), registers as a charitable fundraising platform in California (CNV-LEG-002), and acts as a third-party service provider in Nacha terms (CNV-PAY-001). None of this is operating; no registration was located.
target_answer: Echelon states its regulatory perimeter precisely: it is not a bank, money transmitter, investment adviser or broker-dealer because the platform never holds, controls or executes movement of customer funds, which is enforced by architecture (CNV-LEG-001). It holds the registrations its activities actually require, such as California charitable fundraising platform registration where applicable, and accepts examination by a customer's regulator where law provides for it. A regulatory change log, reviewed by counsel, records changes that affect Echelon or customers and the resulting requirement changes.

title: Disclosure and remediation plans for customer requirements not yet met
status_rationale: This repository records, per answer unit, whether a capability is operating, planned or unknown, but no customer-facing gap register, remediation plan format or progress reporting exists, and no remediation dates have been committed.
target_answer: For each customer requirement Echelon cannot yet meet, Echelon discloses the gap before contract signature using the status of the corresponding answer unit, proposes a compensating control or a dated remediation plan with an accountable owner, records the agreed item in a gap register tied to the contract, and reports progress at an agreed cadence. An item cannot be closed without the evidence named by the answer unit's evidence requirements. Where a customer offers an accommodation path for small suppliers, Echelon uses it rather than overstating its maturity.
current_practice: Not established. Answer unit statuses in this repository are the only existing record of gaps.
intended_practice: Generate the customer gap register from answer unit statuses and contract requirements, with remediation plans added by the accountable owner.
provable: Only the first-party answer unit statuses in this repository; no customer gap register exists.
customer_statement: Echelon will tell you which of your requirements it does not yet meet. A formal gap register with remediation plans and progress reporting is planned.

challenge.customer_intent: The customer wants to know which of its requirements are unmet and whether the vendor will close them, before it relies on the vendor.
challenge.adverse_outcome: A vendor answers yes to requirements it does not meet, and the gap is found after an incident or an examination.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Questionnaire answers are usually self-reported yes or no responses with remediation promised informally; customers rarely track the promises.
challenge.legally_required: No law requires this of Echelon. Supervisory third-party risk guidance expects banks to track vendor issues, which flows to vendors through contracts.
challenge.contractually_required: Some bank supplier documents set remediation deadlines for assessment findings and describe accommodation paths for small suppliers.
challenge.historical_convention: Plans of action and milestones are common in federal security programs and attestation forms.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Not applicable; this is a disclosure and tracking control.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Answer unit status is a controlled field, so a gap can be derived mechanically and an item cannot be reported closed while the underlying status is not operational.
challenge.continuous_evidence: The register extract and the status history of the linked answer units.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Derive customer gap disclosures from answer unit status instead of writing them per questionnaire.

supporting_arguments: Honest gap disclosure is consistent with the operating contract's rule against presenting planned controls as current.
